newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt slips, watching Peru politics, Ecuador.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt slips, watching Peru politics, Ecuador.

text.p: Emerging debt prices slipped Friday, as market players focused on political turmoil in Peru and Ecuador's first-time credit rating on Thursday.
Peruvian Bradies suffered from signs the political crisis around President Alberto Fujimori could be worsening.
"People got a little concerned about the polticial situation," one Brady bond trader said. "We could see some fireworks next week."
In the afternoon, Peru PDI bonds PEPDI=RR dropped 1-1/8 to 64-7/8 and FLIRBs PEFLIRB=RR lost one points to 59-1/4, but dealers said the paper trimmed its losses by the close.
Wall Street would watch how Fujimori addresses the turmoil in his state of the union speech Monday.

Fujimori's popularity has plummeted in recent weeks to its lowest point since he took office in 1990, and a series of scandals involving alleged abuses of power by the security forces have sparked violent street protests.

"In Peru the economic news has been unambiguously positive. The focus has been on the politics, reflected in the way the prices are behaving," Joyce Chang, emerging market debt strategist at Merrill Lynch.

Ecuadorean paper gave back some of the stunning gains it posted Thursday after Moody's Investors Service rated its long-term foreign currency debt at B1, the same level as Argentina and Brazil and one notch above Peru.
Ecuador's PDI bonds slipped 3/8 to 70-1/2, while discount bonds lost 1/4 to 77-3/4.
Analysts looked to the Ecuador rating as offering signs that other nations -- Argentina and Brazil in particular -- could soon win Moody's upgrades.
In addition, the gains by Ecuador may have opened the path for other emerging market assets to gain.
"It makes Russia (debt) looks very cheap," Merrill's Chang said, noting that she also saw value in uncollateralized Brazilian debt, the "C" bonds and global bond due 2027.
One Brady dealer said Ecuador could continue to tighten, another 30 basis points, amid good investor demand.
